use-case: Intake approval closes the use-case stage: the use-case record is written at intake, stored as fields on the registry entry (the Agent Registry pattern) and read by every later gate.
design: The design review is the gate between an approved use case and spending compute; it signs a design record that fixes the oversight model, as in the Human-in-the-loop Gate pattern, and the controls built in.
data: The dataset admission gate asks whether the data may be used and is fit for the purpose; the licence goes into the AIBOM so that a licence change surfaces in the next build.
testing: The eval gate asks whether the system meets thresholds fixed before the tests ran; each test type is a suite behind the Eval Gate in CI.
release: The release gate reads the records the earlier gates produced, including regenerated cards (the Model Card as Control Evidence pattern), and refuses to open while any is missing or stale.
blocked: A failing gate blocks the build: a result below a threshold fixed in advance, or a record that is missing or stale, stops the release.
technical-file: A documentation job assembles the technical file on every release candidate, fails when a row is stale, and emits it as Machine-Readable Evidence (OSCAL) with a human-readable rendering.
